result.title: Hiring Is Changing: Why Human Judgment Still Matters in the AI Era: ManpowerGroup
result.description:
Hiring managers are struggling to find the talent they need, while job seekers face one of the toughest markets in recent memory. Jonas Prising, Chair and CEO of ManpowerGroup, explains what is driving these pressures—from the economic cycle and geopolitical shifts to major demographic changes.

He also examines AI’s growing role in hiring and recruiting. While technology can make the process faster, it does not necessarily make it more accurate. For Prising, human judgment remains essential to recognizing potential, assessing fit and making better hiring decisions.
• How cyclical economic shifts, not structural AI-driven changes, are shaping employer confidence

• How big demographic shifts could push employers to tap underutilized parts of the global workforce

• How AI can increase speed of hiring but not always its accuracy

• How Manpower uses AI in hiring and recruiting and what leaders can learn

Prising also discusses ManpowerGroup’s recent research on employment trends, the early boss that changed how he leads and his take on whether big predictions for the future will become a reality.

Subscribe to Meet The Leader for more conversations on AI, hiring, leadership and the future of work.

result.title: Switzerland’s Solar Railway & Closing Women’s Health Gap | WEF | Stories of the Week
result.description:
This week's top stories of the week include:

00:15 - Switzerland’s solar railway:
Swiss company Sun-Ways lays #solar panels in the space between train tracks. If rolled out across Switzerland’s entire 5,200km rail network, Sun-Ways says, these panels could supply a percentage of the country’s electricity, without leaving any visual or environmental footprint. Here’s how it works.

01:39 - Beaming sunlight at night:
A company is developing satellites with 'giant mirrors' designed to reflect sunlight back to specific locations on Earth after dark. Reflect Orbital says the technology could support solar farms, emergency response and agriculture. But reflecting sunlight into the night sky could also affect astronomy, wildlife, aviation and access to naturally dark skies.

04:05 - Zen in the workplace:
Kacha ‘Shogun’ Mahadumrongkul has been a #Zen monk three times. Now, through his Zenful Institute, he brings its lessons into corporate life. Talking to the World Economic Forum's #MeetTheLeader podcast, he discussed the workplace benefits of #mindfulness, of pausing before you act, and of aligning yourself - and your business endeavours - with your own deepest values.

05:49 - Closing women’s health gap: 
Just 6% of private #healthcare funding goes towards women’s health, and across multiple diseases affecting both sexes, only 3% of studies look at how those diseases affect women. As a result, women are diagnosed late for more than 700 conditions - and spend 25% more of their lives in poorer health than men, a study by the World Economic Forum and McKinsey found.

result.title: The women’s health gap should not exist. Here’s how to close it
result.description:
Just 6% of private #healthcare funding goes towards women’s health, and across multiple diseases affecting both sexes, only 3% of studies look at how those diseases affect women.

As a result, women are diagnosed late for more than 700 conditions - and spend 25% more of their lives in poorer health than men, a study by the World Economic Forum and McKinsey found.

These statistics are shocking - but they’re not set in stone, says Paula Bellostas, Healthcare Global Lead at Kearney and a co-author of a new World Economic Forum paper on women’s #health innovation. She says that closing the women’s health gap means bringing gender into research right from the outset - and women advocating for themselves as patients.

The Women’s Health Innovation Radar, produced in collaboration with the Kearney Health Institute, Gates Foundation, Wellcome Leap and the World Economic Forum’s Global Alliance For Women's Health, maps the biggest advances - and remaining gaps - across the full science-to-patient journey. Read it here: https://www.weforum.org/publications/the-women-s-health-innovation-radar-revealing-gaps-and-opportunities-across-the-science-to-patient-journey/

result.title: AI's real impact on jobs - what it means for you, your company and future generations
result.description:
Artificial intelligence is already having an impact on the way most of us work - but it’s still early days and it's hard to predict exactly which jobs will disappear completely, what new ones will be created, and when and where this will happen.
It’s a subject that's important to all of us - so my colleague Gayle Markovitz spoke to the head of an AI services firm, Ravi Kumar of Cognizant, and to the head of the World Economic Forum’s Centre for the New Economy and Society, Saadia Zahidi. Both have unique insights into the impact of AI on the economy, on employment, and the implications for education and training.

result.title: This start-up wants to provide sunlight at night with mirrored satellites
result.description:
Reflect Orbital is developing satellites with 'giant mirrors' designed to reflect sunlight back to specific locations on Earth after dark.

The company says the technology could power #solar farms at night, provide low-carbon lighting during emergencies and even extend farms' growing seasons.

The technology is still at the experimental stage, and its wider implications remain under debate.
